messages:
maya: FYI a customer (acct: acme-oxford) opened a high-sev — their requests started 403ing after our scheduled key rotation last night. They say desktop app + API calls fail from EU region only. Root starts at ~10:12 UTC.

maya: Error snippet they pasted: `{\"error\":\"invalid_api_key\",\"code\":403}`. Token looks like a rotated API key (starts with rwd_).

maya: Repro steps I ran: curl from our eu-ish host -> 403, curl from us-west -> 200. Leaving here in case infra folks need to jump. @derek @linh

derek: On it. Quick hypothesis: we rewrapped the Vault transit key for eu KMS alias but some pods still have old ciphertext in env or sidecar cache. Will check `secret/data/redwood/api_keys` versions and kube secrets.

linh: Can you paste the curl? also check if CDN edge cached an auth header? normally we don't cache auth but proxy rules can be weird.

maya: here's the curl I used (from eu host):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer rwd_9a3f..." https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response from api-gw:
```
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{\"error\":\"invalid_api_key\",\"request_id\":\"req_1Gq...\"}
```

opsbot: Incident created: INC-202603-194. Tagged infra & vault.

derek: I checked Vault: there are two active versions for the API key path: `secret/data/redwood/api_keys` v3 and v4. v4 was written during rotation and its ciphertext was encrypted with `kms-eu-v2` alias. v3 was `kms-global`. Some pods reference the older `secret` via a legacy annotation `vault.k8s.redwood/skip-rewrap=true` — that skips rewrap. Can you confirm if the deployment has that?

maya: acme-oxford is using our managed integration (iOS SDK + server-to-server) so likely one of our older services still had the annotation. I see `api-service-prod` deployment has the annotation.

linh: That lines up with regional behavior: US requests hit `api-service-prod` nodes that restarted after rotation and pulled v4 ciphertext; EU nodes are sticky to older pods that never rewrapped. So they try to decrypt with `kms-eu-v2` but the ciphertext is for `kms-global` (or vice versa) and transit fails -> we return 403.

derek: Repro locally: fetched kube secret `kubectl -n prod get secret redwood-api-key -o yaml` shows `data.ciphertext` matches v3. Attempting `vault kv get -field=ciphertext secret/data/redwood/api_keys` returned same base64. Trying to decrypt with `kms-eu-v2` -> KMS denied `InvalidCiphertext`.

derek: Quick mitigation: force a restart of EU pods to pick up the new secret and trigger rewrap. Command I plan: `kubectl rollout restart deployment api-service-prod -n prod --context=cluster-eu` and then watch readiness. Any objections? :+1:

maya: Go for it. Tell me when you restart so we can coordinate with customer.

linh: Also suggest removing that `vault.k8s.redwood/skip-rewrap` annotation from the DaemonSet that injects secrets; it was intended for nodes pre-rotation but is now harmful. We should patch the deployment template instead of editing pods individually.

opsbot: Running `kubectl rollout restart` on cluster-eu; starting at 1836003400.

vault-bot: Vault log note: rewrap operation failed for key id `redwood-api-v3` from `kms-eu-v2` at 2026-03-05T10:15:02Z - ciphertext provenance mismatch.

derek: After restart, acme-oxford test request from EU now 200. Also verifying internal logs: earlier requests produced `auth.decrypt_error` traces; after restart no decrypt errors.

maya: Customer confirmed SDK calls OK. Marking impact resolved awaiting postmortem.

linh: Postmortem action items: 1) detect & block `skip-rewrap` annotation during rotate workflow, 2) add a health metric on `vault.decrypt_errors` aggregated by region, 3) update rotation runbook to include `kubectl rollout restart` for regional clusters or use rolling annotator that triggers pod refresh, 4) ensure KMS alias mapping table is included in rotation run output.

maya: I'll open the follow-up ticket and add the customer notes + timeline. Thx team. :relieved:
